text:
maya: FYI eu-west just had a sudden p99 tail spike (20:12) — allocator + kv_evictions look off the charts. suspected tenant?
dan: I'm seeing a tight correlation with egress_burst and kv_evictions/sec. Noticed a tenant (t-982) with many parallel short requests.
sara: t-982 launched a new tiny-batch realtime model yesterday. could be KV cache thrash from long ctx token reuse.
liam: Memory slabs were churning. slab_free -> slab_alloc latency rose, causing per-request stall.
maya: Quick mitigation idea: introduce a per-tenant "queue-shield" (soft concurrency cap) + staggered backoff on slab evictions. Ran a 30m lab run: p99 reduced from 410ms -> 180ms.
dan: numbers?
maya: `lab: shield=120 -> p99=180ms, cpu 7% up, token-cost +1.5%`
liam: tradeoff looks acceptable for SLOs. But warm-pool churn rose marginally, ~2% cold starts.
jordan: Can we auto-move to dedicated pools for repeat offenders? Maybe a 3-strike window.
sara: Dedicated is fine but we need a billing/approval step for non-enterprise tenants. billing-bot: flagged: dedicated-provision will bill tenant owner and our cost center. See https://billing.redwood/prov/txn/444
maya: Proposed flow: (1) soft-shield on default slice when kv_evictions/sec > 75 for 90s; (2) if >3 triggers in 1h -> provision dedicated-slice and shift 40% traffic; (3) continue shield+backoff on default slice until stable.
dan: Automated triggers should be cautious. Suggest a dry-run mode that only alerts on first occurrence.
liam: Also add a fallback route to quantized-compat region model (eu-north) if dedicated capacity not available. Latency up but avoids complete failure.
sara: Need quick cost estimate. maya can you ballpark?
maya: Napkin calc: provisioning 2xsmall-dedicated slice in eu-west ~ $2.4k/month. If we route top 3 noisy tenants -> ~ $7k/mo. SLO fines avoided estimated ~$18k/mo.
jordan: Sounds reasonable. Also add rate-limits per-tenant as a last-resort guard.
maya: Draft runbook snippet for ops channel: ```
- detect: kv_evictions/sec > 75 for 90s
- alert: #eng-infra paged + notify tenant owner
- dry-run: create alert-only incident (5m)
- soft-shield: apply tenant_shield(concurrency=120)
- monitor 15m: if p99 drops -> keep; else after 3 events/1h -> provision dedicated(size=2)
- shift traffic: /route/shift {tenant:t-982, percent:40}
- monitor metrics: p99, kv_evictions/sec, coldstarts/min, egress_bytes
- billing: notify finance & tenant owner
- rollback: if p99 worsens or error rate >1% revert shift
```
ops-bot: created incident U-982 and scheduled a 2h canary window at 23:30 UTC.
dan: I'll run the canary with dry-run enabled first, then promote to auto-evac if results match lab.
sara: I'll prepare a short cost vs SLO spreadsheet and ping account owners.
liam: I'll add telemetry for slab latency and a synthetic that replicates tiny-batch bursts.
jordan: Also consider tagging tenant as noisy=true so we can surface in console and billing.
maya: ok I'll open PR for shield + runbook and own the canary tonight. tagging ops backlog. TL;DR: implement queue-shield + automated soft-evac to dedicated for persistent noisy tenants; canary 23:30 UTC eu-west.
sara: :thumbsup:
dan: :rocket:
ops-bot: canary scheduled (eu-west) — will post summary at end of window
